headline.headline: GILGEOUS-ALEXANDER SILENCES SPURS, THUNDER ROAR BACK TO TIE SERIES
headline.deck: SGA's 30-point masterclass forces a pivotal Game 3 in San Antonio
headline.body:
OKLAHOMA CITY — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander refused to let the Oklahoma City Thunder fall into an early series hole. The reigning MVP poured in 30 points Wednesday night as the Thunder dismantled the San Antonio Spurs 122-113 at Paycom Center, evening the Western Conference semifinals at one game apiece and setting the stage for a raucous Game 3 in San Antonio.

The Thunder, who finished the regular season with the league's best record at 64-18, leaned on Gilgeous-Alexander's trademark blend of craft and aggression to bury a Spurs squad that entered the night riding the momentum of a series-opening victory. Oklahoma City has now demonstrated a familiar resilience — the same club bounced back from series-opening losses twice during last season's championship run, and the blueprint remains intact.

Game 3 shifts to San Antonio with the series dead even, and the Spurs — a 62-20 outfit that finished second in the Western Conference — have shown they will not be swept aside quietly. But after watching Gilgeous-Alexander take over a game with the Thunder's backs against the wall, the rest of the league has been reminded why Oklahoma City is still the team to beat in the West.

secondary.headline: GOLDEN KNIGHTS EXPLOIT MAKAR'S ABSENCE, GRAB 1-0 SERIES EDGE OVER AVALANCHE
secondary.deck: Vegas stuns top-seeded Colorado in Game 1 of the Western Conference finals
secondary.body:
DENVER — The Colorado Avalanche entered the Western Conference finals as the top seed, a 55-16-11 juggernaut built around Cale Makar. But with Makar sidelined by an upper-body injury, the Avalanche looked nothing like that dominant club in Game 1, and the Vegas Golden Knights seized the moment to grab a 4-2 victory and a 1-0 series lead. Goaltender Logan Thompson turned aside 36 shots to backstop the upset, keeping Colorado's attack blunted throughout.

The Avalanche acknowledged a trickle-down effect without their All-World defenseman anchoring the blue line, and the Golden Knights were sharp enough to take full advantage. Vegas, a 39-26-17 club from the Pacific Division, has been battle-tested all spring, and this result signals they are a genuine threat to dethrone Colorado. Game 2 is Friday, and the Avalanche's playoff hopes hinge heavily on Makar's availability.

secondary.headline: REDS ERUPT FOR NINE, HAND PHILLIES A LOPSIDED LOSS AT CITIZENS BANK
secondary.deck: Cincinnati piled on with three-run second and late rallies to rout Philadelphia
secondary.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The Cincinnati Reds came to Citizens Bank Park and left with a thorough 9-4 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies on Wednesday night before a crowd of 38,222. The Reds did their most decisive damage in the second inning, plating three runs to seize control after falling behind 1-0, and Stewart's 12th home run of the season fueled the surge. The Reds added insurance with two more in the seventh and two in the ninth to put the game well beyond reach.

Alec Bohm hit his fifth homer of the year for Philadelphia, but the Phillies' offense could not keep pace with a Cincinnati attack that struck from every corner of the lineup. The game was completed in 2 hours and 48 minutes, leaving the Phillies to regroup before the next meeting. The Reds, with their balanced offensive onslaught, have put the National League on notice.

secondary.headline: EAGLES' NOLAN SMITH ARRESTED AFTER VEHICLE CLOCKED AT 135 MPH IN GEORGIA
secondary.deck: The Eagles linebacker faces speeding and reckless driving charges in the offseason
secondary.body:
ATLANTA — Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Nolan Smith Jr. was arrested and charged with speeding and reckless driving after his vehicle was clocked at 135 miles per hour in Georgia. The arrest marks a jarring offseason distraction for a franchise coming off a run to Super Bowl LX, and it puts Smith in an uncomfortable spotlight at a time when players are expected to stay out of trouble.

Smith, a young pass rusher with considerable upside on Philadelphia's defensive roster, now faces legal proceedings that could carry league discipline as well. The Eagles have not commented publicly on the matter. The NFL offseason has already seen considerable roster and personnel upheaval across the league, and Smith's arrest adds an unwelcome legal dimension to what has been a turbulent spring for several franchises.

column.headline: WITHOUT MAKAR, COLORADO IS JUST ANOTHER TEAM — AND THAT IS VEGAS'S OPENING
column.body:
The Avalanche built their entire postseason identity around Cale Makar. He is not merely a good defenseman — he is the engine, the first mover, the player who transforms Colorado from a very good team into a genuine dynasty candidate. Strip him away, and Game 1 proved exactly what most honest observers suspected: the Avalanche look ordinary. Vegas did not even need to be spectacular. They just needed to be competent, and at 4-2 with 36 saves from Thompson, competent was more than enough.

Gilgeous-Alexander's performance Wednesday night only sharpens the point about what a true franchise cornerstone means in the playoffs. SGA willed Oklahoma City back into the series against a 62-win Spurs club with a single dominant outing. That is the difference between a star and a superstar. The NHL should take note: when you build around one irreplaceable player and that player cannot go, the whole machine seizes up. Colorado has the talent to recover if Makar returns. But Game 2 on Friday is not a luxury — it is a necessity.

story.headline: REDS BATTER PHILLIES 9-4, STEWART HOMER POWERS CINCY SURGE AT CITIZENS BANK
story.deck: Cincinnati erupts for three in the second and two in the ninth to rout Philadelphia
story.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The Cincinnati Reds piled up runs in bunches Wednesday night, beating the Phillies 9-4 at Citizens Bank Park before 38,222 fans in a game that was never truly close after the second inning. DJ Stewart led the charge with his 12th home run of the season, a swing that headlined a three-run second-inning outburst that flipped a 1-0 Philadelphia lead into a Cincinnati advantage for good. The Reds finished with 16 runners left on base, a figure that suggests the margin could have been even wider.

The Phillies briefly made it interesting in the sixth inning, posting three runs to cut Cincinnati's lead to 5-4, with Alec Bohm contributing his fifth home run of the year and Edmundo Sosa adding his second. But the Reds answered immediately, pushing a run across in the same frame and then tacking on two more insurance runs in the ninth on a night when Garrett Dunn collected both a double and a triple. Brandon Lowe, Rhys Hoskins and Bryson Stott also had two-base hits for Philadelphia, but the Phillies could not sustain any rally beyond the sixth.

Philadelphia's Trea Turner, Ranger Suarez's side was kept off-balance throughout, with the Reds' lineup grinding through at-bats and leaving Philadelphia's bullpen taxed by the late innings. The Braves' 9-1 demolition of the Marlins in Miami — fueled by a five-run sixth inning that included home runs by Will Smith and Austin Riley — was the other dominant performance of the evening, but Cincinnati's relentless offensive output across Citizens Bank Park made it the story of the night in the National League.

story.headline: SGA DROPS 30, THUNDER EVEN WESTERN CONFERENCE FINALS AT 1-1
story.deck: Gilgeous-Alexander looks every bit the MVP as Oklahoma City beats San Antonio 122-113
story.body:
OKLAHOMA CITY — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander answered every question Wednesday night, pouring in 30 points to power the Oklahoma City Thunder past the San Antonio Spurs 122-113 and knot the Western Conference finals at one game apiece. The MVP performed like one in front of his home crowd, silencing any doubt that had crept in after the Thunder dropped Game 1 to the second-seeded Spurs.

The final margin of nine points told a story of Oklahoma City control, with the 64-win Thunder leaning on their regular-season pedigree against a San Antonio squad that finished 62-20 and pushed them hard throughout. The Spurs, who stunned OKC in the opener, never found the separation they needed to pull off a second consecutive road win against the league's top team in the Western Conference.

The series now shifts to San Antonio for Game 3, with both clubs fully aware of what is at stake. Oklahoma City has made a habit of bouncing back from series-opening defeats, having done so twice during last season's championship run. Gilgeous-Alexander, praised by commentators including Stephen A. Smith for his urgency and focus, showed the Spurs precisely why he is the standard bearer of this league heading into what promises to be a pivotal Game 3.

boxScores.title: Oklahoma City Thunder 122, San Antonio Spurs 113

story.headline: HART STOPS 36, GOLDEN KNIGHTS STUN AVALANCHE IN GAME 1 WITHOUT MAKAR
story.deck: Vegas takes series lead as Colorado's top defenseman sits with upper-body injury
story.body:
LAS VEGAS — Dylan Coghlan scored his first career playoff goal, Carter Hart turned aside 36 shots, and the Vegas Golden Knights opened the Western Conference Final with a 4-2 victory over the Colorado Avalanche on Wednesday night, taking a 1-0 series lead heading into Friday's Game 2.

The result carried an enormous asterisk in Denver's eyes: star defenseman Cale Makar, the engine of the top-seeded Avalanche's 55-16-11 regular season, was sidelined with an upper-body injury before puck drop. Colorado's players acknowledged afterward that his absence produced a trickle-down effect throughout the lineup, disrupting the puck-movement and transition game that carried the Avs to the conference finals as the Central Division's best team.

Coghlan's goal gave Vegas early momentum and Hart never let it slip, holding firm through a 36-save performance against a Colorado attack that pressed but could not solve him consistently. The Golden Knights, who finished 39-26-17 in the Pacific Division, have now won the opening game of each playoff series they have played this postseason, setting up another pivotal matchup Friday night when the Avalanche will look to even the series and, potentially, welcome Makar back to the ice.

story.headline: QUARTERBACKS ON THE MOVE AS NFL OFFSEASON RESHAPES THE LEAGUE
story.deck: Several franchises gamble on new signal-callers as the roster-building frenzy hits full stride.
story.body:
The dust from Super Bowl LX has barely settled, and already the 2026 NFL offseason has delivered seismic shifts at the quarterback position. The Cleveland Browns, desperate to end years of instability under center, agreed to terms with veteran passer Sam Darnold on a three-year contract worth $112 million, giving the long-suffering franchise a proven starter entering the prime of his career. Meanwhile, the Las Vegas Raiders continued their aggressive retooling by acquiring former Pro Bowl signal-caller Geno Smith from Seattle in exchange for a package of draft picks, signaling a full commitment to contending in the AFC West.

The 2026 NFL Draft last month added fresh fuel to the fire, with the Tennessee Titans selecting Oklahoma quarterback Jackson Fairchild with the second overall pick after a record-breaking college career that drew comparisons to Patrick Mahomes. Fairchild threw for 4,812 yards and 52 touchdowns in his final college season, and Titans head coach Brian Callahan wasted no time declaring the 22-year-old the franchise cornerstone. The New York Giants, picking fourth, countered by nabbing Ohio State edge rusher Damon Pressler, addressing a pass rush that ranked among the league's worst in 2025.

With organized team activities now underway across the league, several training camp storylines are already taking shape. The Dallas Cowboys, who parted ways with Dak Prescott following a disappointing 8-9 season, are holding an open competition between journeyman Kyle Allen and second-year pro Marcus Teel. In New England, first-year head coach Mike Vrabel is installing his aggressive defensive system with a roster that finished last in points allowed a season ago, drawing cautious optimism from a fan base hungry for a return to relevance.
